statements.text: Data centers are a big issue here in Colorado Springs. Let's talk about them. I believe community members should have a voice in the building and location of data centers. Strong and clear guardrails need to be put in place around these companies to protect energy and water usage. Data centers should pay at least their share of energy consumption costs. Jeff Crank, on the other hand, takes campaign donations from AI and data center lobbyists and companies and has sold out his own community by giving AI entities tax breaks and other incentives. I will be a member of Congress who will work to serve YOU- not data center companies.

It is outrageous that AI corporations are not paying their fair share in taxes while we are all left to deal with the very valid concerns and threats AI poses.  Make no mistake—this is a direct result of Crank’s votes. These companies do not need more tax breaks. In Congress, I will focus on regulating AI at the federal level and putting strict guardrails around this industry. Crank, on the other hand, voted to give special tax breaks to data center operators and to prevent states from reining in AI and the big tech companies.  That’s a failure of leadership on his part.
We need to put a check on AI for all of humanity. I generally oppose government overreach, but in this area, strong regulation and oversight are essential,

statements.text: The problems that data centers create are very real. They can drive up electricity prices at a time when El Paso County families can’t afford it. And they require massive amounts of water at a time when Colorado is struggling with a terrible drought,
statements.venue: Written response to The Gazette (Colorado Springs)

statements.text:
You will be shocked to learn that the Trump Super PAC ads against me are filled with lies and misinformation.

So let’s get the facts straight……

Jeff Crank has accepted over $100,000 from lobbyists and special interests tied to data centers, including Project Taurus.  He also voted to give the AI industry $70 billion in tax breaks and undermine state and local regulation of AI.

Unlike Crank, I have not taken any corporate PAC money. I believe local communities should decide if data centers are put in their backyards, and, as an El Paso County resident, I support a moratorium/pause on data centers until we have a better sense of energy and water usage and the threats AI poses to our society.

Trump and Crank will say anything and do anything to hold onto this seat. They are scared. Don’t be fooled by the BS. Only 47 days to go- let’s win this

El Paso County needs a leader they can trust on data centers and so much more. Jeff Crank has proven he sides with Trump and big tech over his constituents. Local communities should decide if data centers are put in their backyards.  There is a lot of uncertainty around AI and data centers right now, and that is why I support a moratorium… we need to take a beat and work to ensure we are doing everything we can to protect El Paso County from higher utility costs, prevent the depletion of our precious water resources, and stop unconstrained AI development.

I think we do need to put some basic guardrails around AI. We have been, we being the federal government, has been behind on these burgeoning industries far too many times. Now we're at AI and it's sort of taking off on a life of its own.

We can't just pretend that AI is here and we can't just say there will be no data centers. That's not realistic. Although I will say as we look at we're in an AI bubble in the stock market right now and what we're seeing right now is that these companies are not turning a profit and I think we should be very circumspect and careful about how we go forward if they're not turning a profit.

I think it is time to put a check on the AI industry. The AI industry itself has asked for that, and there is a role. I'm not a big believer in overregulation, but I think this is a burgeoning industry that needs to have some guardrails set on it around privacy concerns, misuse, loss of control, water and energy usage.
There's a lot of greatness that could come out of AI, but there's a lot of scary stuff, and I think we need to take a beat and take a look at that and actually address it at the federal level.
